To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thermal conductivity of a graphene ribbon with a smooth edge (specularity parameter > 0.7) scales as L(-1/6) for L < 1 μm and as L(-2) for L > 1 μm.
the thermal conductivity of the micrometer-size ribbons with the rough edges scales as L-1/2 and that the thermal conductivity in the bulk graphite scales as log(L).

(i) graphene thermal conductivity scales as L(-1/3) at L < 100 nm, and as L(-0.5) at L > 1 μm; (ii) the thermal conductivity of graphite scales as log(L) at L < ∼30 μ m, and as L (-0.5) for L > 30 μ m.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the thermal conductivity K(L) as a function of ribbon length L in a graphene monolayer and in graphite.
the thermal conductivity of nanostructured graphene and graphite, which is of great fundamental importance for the understanding of the thermal properties of these two-dimensional materials.
the thermal properties of carbon-based nanostructured materials, such as graphite, carbon nanotubes, and graphene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thermal conductivity of a graphene ribbon depends on the lateral dimensions, and the scaling is not monotonic.
the thermal conductivity of a graphene ribbon is expected to be larger than that of a graphite slab of the same lateral size, but smaller than that of a graphene sheet of the same lateral area.
the thermal conductivity of graphite is 2D-like, while that of graphene is 3D-like.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the thermal conductivity of the graphene ribbons and the graphite slabs can be described by the universal formula K(0) + A × L(-n) with the values of the exponents n = 1/2 and n = 1 for the ribbons and slabs, respectively.

the thermal conductivity of the graphene ribbons with the length below ∼1 μm can be significantly higher than that of the bulk graphene, and the thermal conductivity of graphite scales as log(L) for L below ∽30 μm.
the thermal conductivity of a graphene ribbon can be either larger or smaller than that of a graphite slab of the same length depending on the ribbon length.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermal conductivity of the graphene ribbons can be significantly affected by their edges.

, in the absence of the scattering by the defects, the thermal conductivity in the two-dimensional graphene and graphite can be limited by the Umklapp scattering, and the phonons with long wavelengths are the main contributor to the thermal transport in these systems.
the thermal conductivity of the graphene ribbons is strongly influenced by the edge roughness.
